# L1 Rule Catalog

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_docs.py. Do not edit by hand. -->

These are the stable rule IDs accepted by execution-gate `rules`. Missing IDs inherit the shared Rust/Python/API defaults below. Model gates such as `native:pii`, `native:dlp`, `native:injection_l1`, and `native:threat_l1` control complete producers; rule gates control individual entries below.

## PII rules (41)

All PII rules are eligible by default when PII L1 is enabled.

In the default `strict` PII mode every finding scores `1.0`. In `balanced` and `recall` a finding scores the rule base plus the validator strength (checksum 35, format 15, none 0) plus its context, capped at 100 and divided by 100: 25 when the rule binds the value to a field name, otherwise 25/20/15 for a support term of the label near the value and -30 when a counter-context term is nearer (see [PII score and modes](result-schema.md#pii-score-and-modes), [PII context lexicon](#pii-context-lexicon)). Rules marked `proximity (required)` report only with a support term, in every mode. Rules marked `balanced`/`recall` only (K05) report a checksum value without a field name and never run in `strict`; the value must stand alone, not inside a longer number. Structure (K04): a JSON key, a `key: value`/`key=value` line, an XML element or attribute, a CSV header or a Markdown/HTML table header that a `field` rule accepts as its field name binds the value it holds to the rule in every mode, if the value matches the rule's value form in full; for the other rules a key of the label (or a counter-context key) that names exactly the value is its context (+25 or -30) instead of proximity. Obfuscation (K06): every rule also sees values behind zero-width characters, full-width forms and defanged separators (`[.]`, `(@)`) in every mode, and in `recall` also spelled-out e-mail separators (`[at]`, `ät`, `dot`, `punkt`) and numbers spaced character by character (-10); the span is the original text and the validator decides on the normalized value.

### PII context lexicon

The context engine reads these DE/EN entries of `rust/src/detectors/anchor_lexicons/pii.json`; `rust/src/detectors/pii/context.rs` maps them to labels. Support terms of a label count for rules without a field name of their own, a counter-context term counts for every label when it is nearer than every support term. As a structural key (a JSON key, CSV or table header, XML element), a term of either kind names the value it holds; keys are compared lowercased, with `_`, `-`, `.` and camelCase boundaries as spaces, optionally followed by `no`, `nr`, `number` or `nummer`. The key `iban` names no account number.

## DLP regex rules (59)

Rust, Python, and the Ark API enable only credential/secret entity groups by default. Set a rule to `true` to opt into a broader family. Low-level detector `evaluate()` calls bypass gateway execution gates and evaluate the full detector inventory.

Every credential/secret rule drops documented example and test values: a marker word (`EXAMPLE`, `SAMPLE`, `BEISPIEL` or `MUSTER` at the start or end of a word, not inside one such as `resampler`; `TEST`/`TESTKEY`, `FAKE` or `DUMMY` as a whole word; any marker repeated). Values mostly made of repeated chunks or same-character runs are dropped for fixed-format provider, key, hash, JWT, signed-URL and session-ID rules, also when a generic rule captures such a provider-shaped value. Values that need a single sequential run (`AKIA1234567890ABCDEF`) to count as low-variety, and low-variety values of generic credential assignments, are dropped only when the same or one of the three lines above calls the value an example, sample, dummy, fixture or documentation value (DE/EN).

Value-capturing credential rules (assignments, URL parameters and userinfo, signatures, auth headers, cookies, CSRF tokens) also drop placeholders (`<…>`, masks, `TODO`, `CHANGEME`, `REPLACE_ME`, `BITTE_AENDERN`, all-upper or all-lower word sequences such as `YOUR_…_HERE`, `HIER_…_EINTRAGEN`, `YOUR-API-TOKEN`) and references (`$VAR`, `${…}`, `%VAR%`, `{{var}}`, Terraform `var.x`, `os.environ[…]`, `os.Getenv`, `System.getenv`, `Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable`, `ENV.fetch`, `process.env.X` and similar environment accessors). They also drop template syntaxes (`%(name)s`, `{name}`, `%{name}`, `@name@`, `__NAME__`, `!NAME!`, `((name))`, YAML tags such as `!secret` and CloudFormation `!Ref`), secret-manager references (`op://`, `ref+…://`, `@Microsoft.KeyVault(…)`, AWS Secrets Manager/SSM ARNs, GCP `projects/…/secrets/…`, `/run/secrets/…`), `null`/`None`, `changeit`, redaction words (`REDACTED`, `***REMOVED***`, `***ENTFERNT***`) and values that only name the credential (`my-access-token`, `SECRET_PASSWORD`).

Every credential/secret rule also drops the vendor-documented example values of `research/dlp/documented_values.yaml` (stored as SHA-256 of the normalized value) and JWTs with the documented example claims of jwt.io and RFC 7519; publicly known test keys listed there (Hardhat/Anvil default accounts) stay findings with `severity` `test`.

Each rule carries metadata v2, and every entry of `matched_rules` in the layer details reports it: `provider` for provider-bound formats, `validator_strength` (`checksum`: check digits verified; `structure`: decoded or parsed structure verified; `format`: fixed prefix, alphabet, length or syntax shape; `none`: keyword or context only), `source_ref` (`gitleaks:<rule-id>`, vendor or specification URL, or `ark` for in-house rules; see `research/dlp/rule_sources.yaml`) and, for credential/secret rules, `severity` (`test` for provider test/sandbox credentials such as Stripe `sk_test_`, otherwise `live`). Provider, key and JWT rules drop values whose Shannon entropy is below 3.0 bits per character.

Before any regex runs, one Aho-Corasick pass finds the prefilter keywords of all rules (ASCII case-insensitive); a rule whose keywords are absent is skipped. The two rules without a literal have a structural prefilter instead: `dlp_discord_token` needs a run of 24 alphanumerics, `dlp_btc_wif` a run of 51 Base58 characters. Where every match starts a bounded number of bytes before a keyword (for example `dlp_generic_credential_assignment`), the rule is only tried at those positions, in text order. Every gate is proven from the rule's regex, so the findings are the same as a full scan; a text with LONG S or KELVIN SIGN, which case-insensitive rules match for `s` and `k`, runs every rule on the whole text (K07, `rust/tests/dlp_rule_prefilter.rs`).

In the default `strict` DLP mode every finding scores `1.0`. In `balanced` and `recall` (K04, thresholds 0.50 and 0.30 as for PII) a finding scores the rule base plus the validator strength (checksum 35, structure 25, format 15, none 0) plus its context, capped at 100 and divided by 100: 25 for a `field` rule, which captures the value behind a field name of its own; for a `proximity` rule 25/20/15 for a credential term near the value (`dlp.password`, `dlp.credentials`, `dlp.api_key`, `dlp.access_key`, `dlp.access_token`, `dlp.refresh_token`, `dlp.secret_token`, `dlp.client_secret`, `dlp.service_account_key`, `dlp.encryption_key`, `dlp.signing_key`, `dlp.private_key`, `dlp.secret`, `dlp.secret_environment_labels`, `dlp.database_connection`, `dlp.authorization_header`, `dlp.credential_files`) and -30 when a digest, hash or ID term (`dlp.digest_reference`) is nearer; `none` rules score without context. A scored mode keeps the `strict` spans whose score reaches the threshold (see [DLP score and modes](result-schema.md#dlp-score-and-modes)). The score column shows the score without counter-context.
